item.title: A Novel Framework for Addressing Selection Bias in Observational EHR Studies
item.description:
Overview Developing a robust causal inference pipeline specifically designed to construct unbiased cohorts from unstructured, missing-not-at-random (MNAR) electronic health record data.

Problem Motivation Observational healthcare datasets are inherently biased by clinic visitation patterns, leading to severely skewed predictive models.

Methodology Integrated inverse probability weighting (IPW) with deep generative imputation models to synthesize balanced counterfactual data.

Key Findings Reduced selection-induced mortality prediction error by 25% when tested on external, out-of-distribution hospital systems.

item.title: SHAP-based Feature Importance Aggregation Across High-Dimensional Multimodal Datasets
item.description:
Overview A computational methodology designed to aggregate and normalize SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) values when combining tabular EHR data with high-dimensional medical imaging.

Problem Motivation Existing XAI tools struggle to provide unified interpretability metrics across vastly different data modalities (e.g., genetic code vs. pixel maps).

Methodology Developed a tensor-based normalization algorithm that maps localized neural network attributions to a global feature space.

Key Findings Enabled clinicians to cross-reference image-based anomalies directly against specific genomic markers within a unified interface.
